**Nothing here is medical advice.** "Avoid" means *rejected by this pipeline for
systemic use in the affected child*, derived from public literature about a gene, with
no patient data of any kind. It never means "useless in this disease": several agents
below are retained in the record precisely because they are plausible
**tumour**-directed candidates under an entirely separate risk assessment
(ASSUMPTION-DRUG-08). Every row is a research hypothesis requiring pre-clinical
validation.

Source: `knowledge/literature/bub1b/` — mechanism `MECH-BUB1B-01`, gene BUB1B, catalogue
version `bub1b-literature-v1`.

## Read this first: two rejections that look the same and are not

The pipeline rejected every agent below. It did **not** reject them for the same kind of
reason, and collapsing the difference is the fastest way to turn this page into
misinformation.

**OPPOSES — measured, and measured the wrong way.** 5 of 12 agents. Somebody ran the
experiment at this node and the agent moves it away from what the disease needs. That is
a *finding*, and it is disqualifying on the biology.

**Never measured.** 10 of 12 agents have a blank chromosomal-instability cell, and
several also carry an unsigned direction. Nobody has asked. **GP-14: absence of
information is not negative information.** Two mistakes are available here and both are
bad:

- Reading it as a safety finding invents evidence that does not exist. Nobody has shown
  these agents do anything harmful at this node.
- Reading it as reassurance is worse. In a chromosomal-instability syndrome the unasked
  question is disqualifying **by design** (ADR 0011, ASSUMPTION-DRUG-07). An agent in
  this column may be harmless or may be the most dangerous on the page, and the record
  cannot tell you which.

**Measured, and the answer was yes.** 2 agents. The pipeline raises the same
`oncogenic_risk` label for a measured positive as it does for a blank cell, so this page
separates them: the label is identical and the epistemic status is opposite.

The practical consequence is §5 of `docs/track2-hypothesis.md`: the bottleneck in
repurposing for chromosomal-instability disorders is not finding targets. It is that the
safety question that matters most has not been asked of the candidate drugs.

## A. Measured to point the wrong way (5)

For each of these the experiment was done. The direction is a measurement, and it
disagrees with the correction this mechanism requires.

#### Hydroxychloroquine — `DRUG-CQ`

- **Node acted on:** `N9_stress` — Aneuploidy-associated proteotoxic and metabolic
  stress
- **Required correction:** `decrease` — **observed:** `increase` — **verdict:** OPPOSES
  (measured)
- **Chromosomal-instability question:** **never measured**. The chromosomal-instability
  question has **never been asked of this agent**. GP-14: that is not a clean bill of
  health and must never be filled in optimistically. In a chromosomal-instability
  disorder it blocks (ADR 0011, ASSUMPTION-DRUG-07).
- **Rejected for:** `wrong_direction` (all reasons: `wrong_direction`, `oncogenic_risk`,
  `pharmacokinetic_barrier`, `mechanism_mismatch`, `insufficient_evidence`)
- **Why it is dangerous here specifically:** It raises aneuploidy-associated proteotoxic
  and metabolic stress. That is selectively lethal to aneuploid cells, which is exactly
  why the class is attractive against the rhabdomyosarcoma and exactly why it is
  dangerous everywhere else: in this syndrome every tissue is mosaically aneuploid and
  the child is already growth-restricted. Rejected for the soma on the same evidence
  that recommends it for the tumour.

#### Vorinostat — `DRUG-HDAC`

- **Node acted on:** `N5_sac` — Spindle assembly checkpoint signalling
- **Required correction:** `restore` — **observed:** `decrease` — **verdict:** OPPOSES

- **Chromosomal-instability question:** **measured — yes**. The chromosomal-instability
  question **was asked of this agent and the answer was yes**. This is a measurement,

- **Rejected for:** `wrong_direction` (all reasons: `wrong_direction`, `oncogenic_risk`,

  ranking by pathway membership or target closeness that cannot read signs puts an agent
  like this first.

## B. Direction not disqualifying — rejected on an unanswered question (7)

Not one of these was measured to move its node the wrong way. Nicotinamide
mononucleotide was measured to move it the **right** way, at the therapeutic target, and
is rejected anyway. The remaining 6 carry an unsigned direction, which is tri-state and
is **never** rounded to agreement (GP-16): it is a recorded concern and a score penalty,
not a verdict.

What ends all 7 is the same thing — a question with no answer rather than an answer
nobody likes. That is a gate, not a score term, which is why the highest-scoring agent
of the whole run (Nicotinamide mononucleotide, 0.605) is on this page and the accepted
candidate scores lower.

#### Nicotinamide mononucleotide — `DRUG-NMN`

- **Node acted on:** `N3_bubr1` — BubR1 protein abundance
- **Required correction:** `increase` — **observed:** `increase` — **verdict:** agrees
  (measured)
- **Chromosomal-instability question:** **never measured**. The chromosomal-instability
  question has **never been asked of this agent**. GP-14: that is not a clean bill of
  health and must never be filled in optimistically. In a chromosomal-instability
  disorder it blocks (ADR 0011, ASSUMPTION-DRUG-07).
- **Rejected for:** `oncogenic_risk` (all reasons: `oncogenic_risk`, `not_approved`,
  `pharmacokinetic_barrier`, `no_pediatric_evidence`)
- **Why it is dangerous here specifically:** The direction is right — this agent pushes
  the therapeutic target the way the mechanism needs. It is on this page for the
  questions nobody has answered about it, not for its biology, and it is the clearest
  demonstration that the highest-scoring candidate is not automatically the recommended
  one.

#### Dasatinib — `DRUG-SEN`

- **Node acted on:** `N10_clearance` — p53- and p16-dependent arrest, senescence and
  immune clearance of missegregating cells
- **Required correction:** `unknown` — **observed:** `decrease` — **verdict:** cannot
  determine (unsigned)
- **Chromosomal-instability question:** **never measured**. The chromosomal-instability

- **Rejected for:** `oncogenic_risk` (all reasons: `oncogenic_risk`,
  `pharmacokinetic_barrier`, `mechanism_mismatch`, `direction_unknown`)
- **Why it is dangerous here specifically:** It removes p53- and p16-dependent arrest,
  senescence and immune clearance of missegregating cells. In BubR1-hypomorphic mice
  that same response drives the progeroid phenotype *and* suppresses aneuploidy-driven
  tumorigenesis, so removing it in a cancer-predisposed child may remove a barrier
  rather than a burden. The node is flagged compensatory: no corrective direction is
  derived from its state, and the direction check returns cannot-determine rather than
  guessing (ASSUMPTION-MECHANISM-04).

- **Chromosomal-instability question:** **never measured**. The chromosomal-instability

- **Why it is dangerous here specifically:** Its net effect on the stress node in an

#### Nicotinamide — `DRUG-NAM`

- **Node acted on:** `N3_bubr1` — BubR1 protein abundance
- **Required correction:** `increase` — **observed:** `context_dependent` — **verdict:**
  cannot determine (unsigned)
- **Chromosomal-instability question:** **never measured**. The chromosomal-instability
  question has **never been asked of this agent**. GP-14: that is not a clean bill of
  health and must never be filled in optimistically. In a chromosomal-instability
  disorder it blocks (ADR 0011, ASSUMPTION-DRUG-07).
- **Rejected for:** `oncogenic_risk` (all reasons: `oncogenic_risk`,
  `pharmacokinetic_barrier`, `insufficient_evidence`, `direction_unknown`)
- **Why it is dangerous here specifically:** It moves the therapeutic target in both
  directions at once. On this axis that is the NAD+ precursor that is also a sirtuin
  product inhibitor: it feeds the pool SIRT2 consumes and supplies the molecule that
  blocks SIRT2, in the same cell at the same time, and which term dominates at a given
  intracellular concentration has never been measured in any genotype. A
  context-dependent sign is worse than a missing one for a first experiment, because it
  destroys interpretability in both outcomes: a rise in BubR1 cannot distinguish NAD+
  supply from an off-axis effect, and a fall cannot distinguish a wrong mechanism from
  having inhibited the enzyme the mechanism runs on. The only direct measurement of this
  agent class on this endpoint runs the wrong way — the sirtuin-inhibiting concentration
  lowered BubR1 protein — at an exposure well above anything a patient reaches, which
  fixes the sign of the inhibitory arm without fixing the dose at which it wins.
